title: High Altitude Whistle
hook: What happens if you whistle at high altitude?

beats.label: 1000 M
beats.line: At 1000 meters, your lungs work normally, and the whistle sounds clear.
beats.idea: Character whistles happily; sound waves travel smoothly in clean air.

beats.label: 3000 M
beats.line: At 3000 meters, thin air makes breaths feel shallow, and your whistle sounds quieter.
beats.idea: Character inhales visibly; chest expands; sound waves look slightly denser but still travel.

beats.label: 5000 M
beats.line: At 5000 meters, low oxygen makes your heart beat faster to keep you safe.
beats.idea: Close-up of heart beating rapidly; character’s face flushes slightly; sound waves wobble.

beats.label: 8000 M
beats.line: At 8000 meters, cold air slows sound, so your whistle sounds deeper.
beats.idea: Sound waves stretch out and slow down; character looks confused by the pitch change.

description: A character whistles on a mountain, showing how thinning air affects sound and breathing.

facts.claim: Air density decreases with altitude, reducing the speed of sound.
Lower oxygen levels at high altitude increase heart rate and breathing rate.

end.line: Would you try whistling up there?

topic: What happens if you whistle at high altitude?
